In The Urantia Book, the relationship among matter (energy), mind, and spirit is described as the core threefold system for understanding both the structure of the whole universe and the immortal eternal life of human beings.

1. The Origin and Cosmic Attributes of the Threefold Reality

Matter (energy / things / facts)

Origin and nature: All physical energy and matter go forth from the Isle of Paradise (nether Paradise) as their source and respond to the circuits of linear gravity and to the physical laws of the universe [11:5.9, 12:8.2, 12:8.10].

Cosmic attributes: It is the nonspiritual, foundational domain that makes up the "things" and "facts" of universe reality, together with its mechanical mechanisms [9:4.5, 12:8.10, 101:5.2, 103:6.6].

Mind (intelligence / meanings / wisdom)

Origin and nature: Mind is an endowment derived from the Third Source and Center, the Infinite Spirit, and from cosmic mind [9:1.1, 9:4.3, 12:8.6, 12:8.11].

Cosmic attributes: It deals with the "meanings" of universe reality and acts as the mediator that interprets and bridges the gap between material facts and spiritual values [9:4.5, 101:5.8, 103:6.6].

Spirit (divinity / values / purpose)

Origin and nature: Spirit is the highest personal reality, going forth from the Universal Father and the Eternal Son [6:2.6, 12:8.4, 12:8.12].

Cosmic attributes: It stands for the "values" and the "divine purpose" of universe reality and is the eternal final goal toward which personal beings should strive [9:4.5, 12:8.12, 12:8.13].

2. The Hierarchy of Energy, Mind, and Spirit and the Mechanism of Control

The threefold cosmic hierarchy: In cosmic relationships the physical systems are subordinate, the mind systems are co-ordinate (cooperative), and the spirit systems are directive [112:2.1, 116:6.1].

The control of matter by mind: Mind does not of itself directly create or control energy, but it controls and dominates energy by intelligently manipulating physical laws and mechanical mechanisms and by using them wisely [42:11.1, 111:6.4, 111:6.5].

The dominance of spirit over mind: Spirit does not manipulate matter directly but presents spiritual values and goals to the mind [111:6.4, 116:6.1]. When the human free will chooses spirit leading, spirit dominates mind and spiritualizes the material self [1:3.7, 42:12.15, 116:6.1].

3. Human Experience and the Birth of the Immortal (Morontia) Soul

The material mind as the arena of choice: The material mind of man is the arena of will in which decisions are made between good and evil, between spirit and flesh [111:1.3].

The birth of the morontia soul: When the material mind of the mortal, co-operating with the indwelling Thought Adjuster (the spirit of God), chooses the divine will, a third, supermaterial reality, the immortal morontia soul, is newly formed by the union of these two factors [111:2.2, 111:2.7].

The transfer of identity: The material self perishes at death, but the morontia soul, bearing spiritual values, unites with the Thought Adjuster and attains eternal life [1:3.7, 111:2.10, 112:2.20].

4. The Academic Unification of Science, Philosophy, and Religion

Science (facts): It explores the physical facts of matter and energy [101:2.8, 101:5.2, 103:6.9].

Philosophy (meanings): Through the reason and wisdom of mind it co-ordinates facts and values and establishes meanings [101:5.2, 102:3.5, 103:6.9].

Religion (values): Through spiritual faith and worship it experiences divine values and sonship with God [101:2.8, 101:5.2, 103:6.9].

Unification through revelation: True revelation harmonizes the facts of science, the wisdom of philosophy, and the values of religion into one, giving man cosmic-philosophical unity and peace [101:2.1, 101:2.8, 103:6.15].

q081.question: Please tell me in detail about the beings in The Urantia Book who transform energy into matter and are responsible for controlling all the energy of the universe.
q081.answer:
According to The Urantia Book, the beings who transform nonspiritual space potency into primordial force, raise it stage by stage until it condenses into actual matter (ultimatons, electrons, atoms), and direct and control all the physical energies of the grand universe form the following elaborate hierarchy.

1. Master Force Organizers

These are the supreme beings who are resident on nether Paradise and go out into the outer reaches of space in the vast master universe where matter is not yet organized, activating energy and leading the earliest stages that precede materialization [29:5.1, 42:2.4].

Primary Eventuated Master Force Organizers: They stir up cyclones in the space potency (absoluta) of the Unqualified Absolute, changing it into pure primordial force (segregata) and then into the stage of puissant energy [29:5.5, 42:2.6, 42:2.7, 42:2.11].

Associate Transcendental Master Force Organizers: They transform puissant energy into gravity energy, which responds to gravity (ultimata), and condense it so that the ultimaton, the basic particle of matter, comes into being [15:4.2, 29:5.5, 42:2.12]. When the energy reaches the stage at which it is fully responsive to the gravity and linear-gravity circuits, they hand over its management to the power directors [15:4.2, 29:5.6, 42:2.12].

2. Seven Supreme Power Directors

These are quasi-material beings jointly created by the Seven Master Spirits of Paradise, the supreme leaders who have overall charge of the control of physical energy throughout the grand universe [29:1.1]. Stationed on the periphery of Paradise, they direct the control of physical power throughout all the universes [29:1.3].

3. Supreme Power Centers

These beings are produced by the Seven Supreme Power Directors and the Seven Master Spirits; they are tertiary personalities of the Infinite Spirit family endowed with high intellectual qualities [29:2.1, 29:2.9]. They serve as living power intelligences that organize undifferentiated energy into electronic physical power and direct its course [29:2.9, 29:2.13].

In keeping with the structure of the grand universe, they are divided into seven groups (supreme center supervisors, Havona centers, superuniverse centers, local universe centers, constellation centers, system centers, and unclassified centers), each controlling the power circuits of its own domain [29:2.1, 29:2.2, 29:2.3, 29:2.4, 29:2.5, 29:2.6, 29:2.7, 29:2.8].

4. Master Physical Controllers

These are the offspring of the Supreme Power Centers, the executive agents who move directly through the space of the grand universe and actually manipulate, transform, transmit, and maintain energy [29:4.1, 29:4.4]. They are divided into seven orders in all:

Associate Power Directors: They assign the physical controllers to the local systems and planets and manage and inspect them [29:4.15, 29:4.17].

Mechanical Controllers: Using their powerful antigravity endowments, they determine the direction of energy currents and equalize the energy pressures of systems and planets [29:4.19, 29:4.20].

Energy Transformers: As living switches, they freely change the form and potential of the physical energies of space [29:4.22, 29:4.24, 29:4.25].

Energy Transmitters: They act as living superconductors, linking the energy circuits between universes and planets and boosting their signals [29:4.27, 29:4.28, 29:4.29].

Primary Associators: They store and conserve energy and, working with atoms, electrons, and ultimatons, serve as catalysts in producing the first units of primitive matter [29:4.32, 29:4.33].

Secondary Dissociators: These are the alchemists of space who, using their enormous antigravity properties, liberate boundless energy from matter [29:4.35].

Frandalanks and Chronoldeks: These are living, intelligent mechanisms that automatically and accurately measure and register the status, mass, velocity, and time of universe force-energy [29:4.36, 29:4.37].

5. Morontia Power Supervisors

These beings are created by the Local Universe Mother Spirit; they associate physical and spiritual energies to organize and supply the one hundred forms of morontia material, the transitional reality between matter and spirit [48:1.3, 48:2.1, 48:2.2]. (They work in seven specialized divisions: circuit regulators, system co-ordinators, planetary custodians, combined controllers, liaison stabilizers, selective assorters, and associate registrars) [48:2.3, 48:2.4, 48:2.5, 48:2.6, 48:2.7, 48:2.8, 48:2.9, 48:2.10].

q082.question: Please explain in detail the structure and cohesion of the atom.
q082.answer:
The structure of the atom and the mechanism of its cohesion, as described in The Urantia Book, are explained in terms of a solar-system-like order and a finely tuned interplay among microscopic particles. Here is a summary of the main points, divided into two aspects: structure and cohesion.

1. The Basic Structure of the Atom and the Arrangement of Electrons

Solar-system-like structure and microscopic proportions:

Every atom is formed in a manner resembling the order of a solar system. Around a relatively stationary central nucleus (protons and neutrons), the electrons whirl about in vast circuit orbits.

The diameter of an atom is a little more than one one-hundred-millionth of an inch. The negatively charged electron weighs slightly more than one two-thousandth of the hydrogen atom, the lightest atom, while the proton, though of about the same size as the electron, weighs some 2,000 times as much as the electron.

The 100 atomic configurations (the decimal system):

The local universe (Nebadon) is organized on the decimal system, so the maximum configuration is a total of 100 possible atomic forms, with anywhere from 1 to 100 electrons revolving around the central nucleus.

The internal stability of an atom is determined by the number of electrically inactive neutrons in the central nucleus.

The four zones of electron orbits (electron families): The electrons in an atom function in four zones according to their distance from the central nucleus.

The innermost 30 electrons: They are so close to the nucleus that their energies intermingle, making them difficult to observe or identify as individual particles.

The second 30 electrons: They possess a developing individuality and exercise more complete control over the energy system.

The third 30 electrons: They are still more individualized and circulate in distinct and definite orbits.

The outermost 10 electrons: These are present only in the ten heaviest elements. Being somewhat free from the control of the mother nucleus, they can easily escape its grip with only a slight change in temperature or pressure (for example, the spontaneous disintegration of uranium).

2. The Mechanism of Atomic Cohesion and Bonding

The space within the atom and attraction:

The space between the electrons within the atom is not entirely empty; it is activated by wave phenomena perfectly synchronized with the velocity of the electrons and the revolutions of the ultimatons.

Although attraction is one factor that sustains the atomic system, linear attraction alone cannot fully explain the powerful binding force of the atom.

The exchange action of the meson and the stability of the nucleus:

The positively charged protons gathered in the atomic nucleus ought, by their electric repulsion, to fly apart from one another and destroy the nucleus, but they are held firmly together by a particle called the meson.

The meson is an energy-carrying particle 180 times heavier than the electron. For an extremely brief fraction of a second, it shuttles back and forth continuously between protons and neutrons, transferring electric charge.

Because of this exceedingly rapid shuttling of charge, a given particle momentarily changes back and forth between the state of a proton and that of a neutron, so that the destructive electric repulsion of the protons is neutralized and the atomic nucleus is kept stable.

Radioactive decay and the unexplained cohesive force:

The reason radioactive elements release more energy than expected when they disintegrate spontaneously is that this meson (the energy carrier) breaks down into a simple electron.

The meson explains the bond between protons and neutrons, but the pure cohesion of proton to proton and of neutron to neutron is yet another powerful form of energy that the science of Urantia (the earth) has not yet discovered

q083.question: Please explain quantum energy waves and the spectrum of 100 octaves of wave energy.
q083.answer:
Here are the details of the mechanism of quantum energy waves within the atom and of the 100-octave spectrum of wave energy, as revealed in Paper 42 of The Urantia Book.

1. How Quantum Energy Waves Operate within the Atom

Emission and absorption in quantum units: In the realms of matter, energy does not flow continuously; it is emitted or absorbed only in exact "quantum" units or in multiples of them.

Electron orbit shifts and the generation of waves: When an electron within the atom moves to a higher or lower energy orbit, or when electrons collide with one another, light energy is emitted or absorbed in quantum units. The vibration and wavelike behavior of the units of energy that arise at such times are determined entirely by the dimensions of the material structures concerned.

The precise ratio of the wavelength (the law of 860 times): The wavelength of the wavelike energy ripples emitted within the atom is exactly 860 times the diameter of the ultimaton, electron, atom, or other energy unit concerned.

The phenomenon of wave superimposition: The physical confusion that arises in observing quantum behavior is due to the superimposition of energy waves upon one another in space. When two wave crests meet, they form a crest of double height, but when a crest meets a trough, they cancel each other and the wave disappears.

The activation of the space within the atom: The space between the atomic nucleus and the electrons is not empty; it is activated and kept in balance by wave phenomena perfectly synchronized with the velocity of electronic circulation and with the axial revolutions of the ultimatons.

2. The 100-Octave Spectrum of Wave Energy

In the superuniverse of Orvonton there exists a spectrum of wave energy totaling 100 octaves, which makes up the whole of the physical energy of the universe.

The limits of human perception: Of the full 100-octave spectrum, the science of Urantia (the earth) recognizes 64 octaves, partially or wholly. In particular, the visible light that the human eye can perceive occupies only one octave (the 46th octave) of these 100.

The overall structure of the wave-energy spectrum:

The solar-ray spectrum: It occupies 4 octaves of the whole scale and includes visible light (the 46th octave), ultraviolet rays, and others.

The region above visible light: Ten octaves above the ultraviolet lie the X rays and gamma rays, and the uppermost 32 octaves are the zone of the powerful cosmic rays that pour in from outer space.

The region below visible light: Below visible light lie the infrared rays, and beneath them the lowest 30 octaves consist of the Hertzian waves (the radio-transmission group) used for broadcasting and communication.

3. The Ten Classifications of Wave Energy from the Standpoint of Urantia Science

The Urantia Book divides the wave energies that can be observed and classified at the level of the earth, out of the 100-octave spectrum, into ten stages:

Sub-ultimatonic rays: Waves at the borderline stage where ultimatons begin to take definite form.

Ultimatonic rays: Vibrations produced just before ultimatons assemble in space and condense into electronic matter.

Short cosmic rays: The shortest electronic vibrations of the pre-atomic stage, associated with the birth and destruction of atoms.

The electron stage: The basic waves of ordinary materialization, emitting quanta when electrons shift orbits or collide.

Gamma rays: Waves emitted when atomic nuclei split spontaneously, as in the disintegration of radium.

The X-ray group: Electromagnetic disturbance waves produced when the velocity of an electron is suddenly arrested or slowed.

Ultraviolet rays: The chemical rays and mechanical products of the sun.

White light: The whole of the visible light seen by the human eye.

Infrared rays: Slowing waves of electronic activity passing over into the stage of perceptible heat.

Hertzian waves: The wavelengths used for radio and broadcast transmission.

Thus, from the wave motion of quanta within the microscopic atom to the immense cosmic wave spectrum of 100 octaves, every physical wave shows that the energy emanating from Paradise is precisely controlled according to universal law.

q084.question: Please also tell me about "the reality of the ether hypothesis and its behavior in space" when wave energy passes through space, and about "the actual operations of the physical controllers who handle energy-matter."
q084.answer:
Here is a summary of "the reality of the ether hypothesis and its behavior in space" and "the actual operations of the Master Physical Controllers," as described in The Urantia Book.

1. The Reality of the Ether Hypothesis and Its Behavior in Space

The nonexistence of the ether as a hypothetical medium: According to The Urantia Book, the "ether," assumed by science to be an independent material medium, does not exist. The ether spoken of by human science is merely a collective name for the whole of the force and energy activities that fill space.

The straight-line travel of energy particles and wave phenomena: All forms of energy particles (ultimatons and electronic aggregations), such as light and electromagnetic waves, actually travel through space in straight lines. However, when the energy particles moving at high velocity encounter the force blanket (resistance) of space and the tensions of attraction, "disturbances within space" arise. Much as waves form when a ship cuts through water, or as raindrops look like ripples when the wind blows, these phenomena of illusion and superimposition cause the motion to be observed as wave motion.

The cosmic importance of the absence of an ether: If a fixed ether medium existed and produced frictional resistance, the inhabited planets would eventually be drawn into their suns and destroyed, and the electrons would be sucked into the atomic nucleus. It is because there is no hypothetical ether that heavenly bodies and microscopic particles can continue in stable orbital motion.

2. The Actual Operations of the Master Physical Controllers

The Master Physical Controllers are living, intelligent controllers who directly transform, regulate, maintain, and transmit the physical energies within space; they operate in seven orders in all.

Associate Power Directors: In keeping with changes in the physical conditions of the realms, they assign the various physical controllers to the planets, systems, and universes where they are needed and inspect them.

Mechanical Controllers: Possessing a powerful endowment of antigravity, they equalize the energy pressures of the universe circuits and facilitate the flow of energy. Ten of them are also resident on Urantia (the earth), and together with 1,000 energy transmitters they provide the initial antigravity propulsion when angels take off from the planet (seraphic transport).

Energy Transformers: As living switches, they freely change the form and potential of 27 of the 30 energies of space. They maintain physical equilibrium by insulating a particular planet from excessive energy streams pouring from great stars or neighboring planets, or by storing up and releasing energy.

Energy Transmitters: They serve as living superconductors, linking up the delicate energy channels and lines of communication that run from one planet to another. By reinforcing faint signals received from great distances, they maintain universe broadcasts and emergency communication networks.

Primary Associators: Masters of energy conservation and storage, they store up energy and act as catalysts in handling atomic, electronic, and ultimatonic particles, producing the primitive units of matter.

Secondary Dissociators: These are the "alchemists of space," who use their powerful antigravity qualities to break down matter and release the boundless energy condensed within it.

Frandalanks and Chronoldeks: Rather than directly manipulating physical energy, they are living, intelligent measuring mechanisms that automatically and accurately gauge and record the state, mass, pressure, and velocity of universe force-energy and its temporal precision.

q085.question: What are the ten classifications of matter existing in the universe according to The Urantia Book?
q085.answer:
According to Paper 42 (Energy—Mind and Matter) of The Urantia Book, the ten grand divisions of matter existing in the various suns, planets, and heavenly bodies of the universes of time and space, excluding the central universe, are as follows.

Ultimatonic matter: The most basic physical unit of material existence; the energy particles that make up the electron.

Subelectronic matter: The explosive and repellent stage of the solar supergases.

Electronic matter: The electrical stage of material differentiation, including electrons, protons, and various other units entering into the varied constitution of the electronic groups.

Subatomic matter: Matter existing extensively in the interior of the hot, blazing suns.

Shattered atoms: The form found in the cooling suns and throughout space.

Ionized matter: Individual atoms stripped of their outer, chemically active electrons by electrical, thermal, or X-ray activities or by the action of solvents.

Atomic matter: The chemical stage of elemental organization, the component units of molecular or visible matter.

The molecular stage of matter: A relatively stable state of materialization under ordinary conditions, the matter existing on the earth (Urantia).

Radioactive matter: Matter exhibiting the tendency and activity of the heavier elements to disintegrate spontaneously under conditions of moderate heat and diminished gravity pressure.

Collapsed matter: Matter found in the interior of cold or dead suns, in which the ultimatonic and electronic units are packed together very densely and their revolutions are greatly slowed.

This classification is based not so much on the outward appearance seen by an outside observer as on the internal organization of energy and the physical properties of matter.

q086.question: Please tell me in detail about the relationship among the Triodities, the three Absolutes, and the Supreme Being.
q086.answer:
According to The Urantia Book, the three Absolutes, the Triodities, and the Supreme Being are key concepts that explain the actualities and potentials of the universe and the emergence of the evolving Deity of time and space, and they are deeply interrelated.

1. The Three Absolutes

The three Absolutes existing in the universe are the three absolute presences embodying infinite potential and reactivity and the balance between them.

Deity Absolute: It contains all divine potentials and the possibilities of Deity, and is the potential reservoir in which all divinity activities take place.

Unqualified Absolute: It is undeified and impersonal, the static, reactive, infinite realm of potential of space, force, and energy.

Universal Absolute: It is the associative co-ordinator that adjusts the divinity-tension between deified reality (the Deity Absolute) and undeified reality (the Unqualified Absolute), equalizing and unifying the difference between actuality and potentiality.

2. The Structure of the Triodities

The Triodities are threefold associations of absolute realities in which the Universal Father is not directly included as a personal member. The Triodities fall into two main kinds.

Triodity of Actuality

Composition: The Eternal Son (the absolute of spirit) + the Isle of Paradise (the absolute cosmic and physical pattern) + the Conjoint Actor/Infinite Spirit (the absolute of mind and the synthesis of Deity).

Role: It co-ordinates the sum total of all absolute realities already actualized, whether spiritual, cosmic, or mindal.

Triodity of Potentiality

Composition: Deity Absolute + Universal Absolute + Unqualified Absolute (the association of the three Absolutes themselves).

Role: It correlates and unifies the infinity reservoirs of all latent energies and realities, spiritual, mindal, and cosmic, not yet manifested.

3. The Relationship among the Triodities, the Three Absolutes, and the Supreme Being

The Supreme Being is the experiential Deity who grows in time and space by synthesizing power and personality in the evolutionary universes. Their relationship can be summed up along the following three key axes.

The direct agency in the emergence of experiential Deity: Whereas the Trinities are chiefly concerned with the functional unification of infinity, the Triodities are directly concerned with the cosmic appearance of experiential Deities such as the Supreme Being and with their power-personality synthesis.

The transformation from potential into actual: The Supreme Being is the culmination and focus of the process by which, at the finite universe level, the Triodity of Actuality (the actuals) and the Triodity of Potentiality (the three Absolutes) interact, and the infinite potentials contained in the three Absolutes are transformed into actualities in time and space (the power-personality synthesis).

Distinguishing the origins of personality and of power

The origin of spirit personality: The spirit personality of the Supreme Being is absolutely dependent upon, and derived from, the Paradise Trinity.

The origin of almighty power: The almighty power of the Supreme Being (the Almighty Supreme) and his growth are grounded in the two Triodities (the Triodity of Actuality + the Triodity of Potentiality of the three Absolutes), together with God the Sevenfold and the experiential achievements of the creatures and Creators of time and space.

The two-directional movement of growth: The growth of the Supreme Being shows a double movement, directed inward (intensively) toward Paradise and Deity and at the same time outward (extensively) toward the infinite space and potential held by the three Absolutes (the Triodity of Potentiality).

In the end, the three Absolutes constitute the "Triodity of Potentiality" and conserve all the possibilities of the universe, and as this combines with the Triodity of Actuality and the creative activities of time and space, the actualization of the Supreme Being, the evolving finite God, becomes possible

q087.question: Please tell me in detail about the triunities.
q087.answer:
According to Paper 104 of The Urantia Book, a triunity is a functional association formed with the Universal Father, the origin of the universe and the First Source and Center, as its original member.

1. The Difference between the Trinity and the Triunities

The triunities are strictly distinguished from the Paradise Trinity, which is a union of Deity itself, as follows:

The Paradise Trinity: The indivisible, organic union of the three Deities, the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, and the Infinite Spirit, constituting a single Deity reality.

The triunities: Functional groupings and associations in which not only personal Deity but also the impersonal absolutes (the Isle of Paradise, the Unqualified Absolute, the Deity Absolute, the Universal Absolute, and so on) take part.

The functional balance wheel: Even though the Universal Father has differentiated his infinity into the seven Absolutes, he maintains the functional unity of the whole of infinity through the association of the triunities, and therefore they are called "⟦Q 104:4.46⟧the functional balance wheel of infinity⟦/Q⟧."

2. The Seven Triunities

There are fifteen triunity associations in all in which the First Source and Center takes the lead; the composition and main roles of the seven triunities that have been revealed are as follows:

The First Triunity: the personal-purposive triunity

Composition: Universal Father + Eternal Son + Infinite Spirit

Role: As the threefold union of love, mercy, and ministry, it expresses the infinity of the will of personal Deity and carries on the ministry of revealing Deity to creatures.

The Second Triunity: the power-pattern triunity

Composition: the Father-Son + the Isle of Paradise + the Conjoint Actor (Infinite Spirit)

Role: It produces all the material and physical patterns and configurations of the universe, from the smallest ultimaton to the whirling nebulae and the grand universe.

The Third Triunity: the spirit-evolutional triunity

Composition: Universal Father + the Son-Spirit + the Deity Absolute

Role: It governs the origin, expression, and final destiny of all spiritual manifestations and values in the universe, from spirit potential to the pure spirit of Paradise.

The Fourth Triunity: the triunity of energy infinity

Composition: the Father-Spirit + the Isle of Paradise + the Unqualified Absolute

Role: It absolutely controls and supplies all force and energy realities of the cosmos, from space potency to the living, nonspiritual energy of Paradise (monota).

The Fifth Triunity: the triunity of reactive infinity

Composition: Universal Father + the Universal Absolute + the Unqualified Absolute

Role: Within the domain of nondeity reality, it establishes the capacity to react without limit to the volitional, causative, and patterning acts of the other triunities.

The Sixth Triunity: the triunity of cosmic-associated Deity

Composition: Universal Father + the Deity Absolute + the Universal Absolute

Role: As the last outreach of divinity toward the realms beyond the deified, it unites the cosmic immanence and the transcendence of Deity.

The Seventh Triunity: the triunity of infinite unity

Composition: Universal Father + the Conjoint Actor + the Universal Absolute

Role: It universally unifies, on the infinite level, all actualized and potential realities, from the finite to the absolute.

3. The Difference from the Triodities

The unrevealed triunities: There are eight additional triunities concerned with realities and destinies beyond the experiential level of supremacy, but they have not been revealed to human beings.

The distinction from the triodities: Associations in which the Universal Father is directly included as an original member are called triunities, whereas threefold associations formed among the Son, the Isle, the Infinite Spirit, or the Absolutes, without the Father being directly included (for example, the Triodity of Actuality and the Triodity of Potentiality), are called triodities.

q088.question: Please tell me about morontia and explain the relationship among matter, mind, and spirit.
q088.answer:
The concept of morontia and the relationship among matter, mind, and spirit form a central axis of the cosmology of The Urantia Book, explaining both the levels of reality in the universe and the principles of the human ascension process.

1. The Definition and Characteristics of Morontia

Concept and dimension: Morontia designates the vast transitional reality and transition realm that exists between the physical level and the spirit level. It is the intermediate stage of the ascension process that leads from the material mortal state to full spirit status.

Structural nature: The warp of morontia is spiritual, and its woof is physical (material). It may be personal or impersonal reality, and it may be living or nonliving energy.

Morontia matter and the morontia worlds: On the morontia worlds (the architectural spheres) there exist, in addition to the 100 elements of ordinary matter, 100 forms of distinctive morontia material, which the morontia power supervisors organize by combining material energies with spiritual energies. During the local universe career the ascending human passes successively through 570 morontia body changes and is progressively spiritualized.

The morontia soul: The immortal self that is born when the material mind of the mortal and the indwelling divine spirit (the Thought Adjuster) co-operate in choosing eternal values; its nature is a morontia reality.

2. The Concepts of Matter, Mind, and Spirit and Their Threefold Relationship

The universe is composed of three basic levels of reality, matter (energy—things), mind (intellect—meanings), and spirit (divinity—values), which are unified in personality.

① Matter (Physical Energy)

Definition: Organized energy that is subject to linear gravity and is conditioned by motion and mind.

Cosmic meaning: In the universe, matter corresponds to "things," and its original source is the Isle of Paradise.

Role: It is the stage on which spiritual activities take place and the physical echo left by the creative acts of spirit-mind.

② Spirit

Definition: The highest personal reality and divine value, which transcends physical gravity and responds only to spiritual attraction.

Cosmic meaning: In the universe, spirit corresponds to "value" and "purpose," and its source is the Eternal Son.

Role: It is the fundamental reality of all creature personality experience, the immortal goal of existence, and its architect.

③ Mind

Definition: An organized system of consciousness that is not wholly subject to material gravity and that mediates and co-ordinates between spirit and matter.

Cosmic meaning: In the universe, mind corresponds to "meaning," and its source is the Infinite Spirit (the Conjoint Actor).

Role: Mind alone serves as the channel that interrelates and connects the physical forces of the material level with the spiritual values of the spirit level.

3. The Interaction and Integration of Matter, Mind, and Spirit

An analogy for their roles: Compared to building, spirit is the architect, mind is the builder, and the body (matter) is the building.

The transformation of value and meaning: Mind translates the divine "values" of spirit into intellectual "meanings," and the will brings the meanings of mind to actual fruition in the material and spiritual realms.

Morontial integration within personality: When the mind, the stage of self-consciousness of the human personality, makes moral and spiritual choices under the guidance of spirit, a new reality called the morontia soul comes into being at the meeting point of the material foundation and spiritual influence, and it finally attains to eternal survival.

q089.question: Please tell me the process from the time of Andronover, 987 billion years ago, until the local universe of Nebadon came into being.
q089.answer:
According to Paper 57 of The Urantia Book, the main stages from the earliest formation of the Andronover nebula until the local universe of Nebadon was officially established and registered are as follows.

1. 987 to 900 billion years ago: Initial exploration and cosmic authorization

987 billion years ago: An associate force organizer of the Orvonton superuniverse series (number 811,307) reported to the Ancients of Days on Uversa, the superuniverse capital, that space conditions in the eastern sector of Orvonton were favorable for the initiation of materialization phenomena.

900 billion years ago: As the Uversa Council of Equilibrium issued an official permit, the force organizers and their staff set out on their journey to the eastern space sector to organize a new physical creation.

2. 875 to 600 billion years ago: The initiation of the nebula and the primary nebular stage

875 billion years ago: The enormous Andronover nebula (number 876,926) was officially initiated, and a revolving energy whirl (space cyclone) was set in motion by the force organizers.

800 billion years ago: The Andronover creation was established as one of the magnificent primary nebulae of Orvonton.

700 to 600 billion years ago: The nebula grew rapidly, its energy aggregation reached its peak 600 billion years ago, and it became a vast gas cloud in the shape of a flattened rotating spheroid.

3. 500 to 400 billion years ago: The secondary spiral-nebula stage and Michael's choice

500 billion years ago: As the Andronover nebula began to take on a spiral form, the first sun escaped the gravity of the mother mass and was thrown out into space.

400 billion years ago: As the central mother nucleus of the nebula condensed, it entered a stage of recapturing the surrounding suns.

The selection of the Nebadon domain (about 400 billion years ago): Michael of Nebadon (Christ Michael), a Paradise Creator Son, chose the region of the disintegrating Andronover nebula as the site of his adventure in universe building and began to organize it.

The building of the headquarters spheres: Immediately after this choice, construction began on Salvington, the capital of the local universe, with its architectural worlds, and on the group of one hundred constellation headquarters planets; the work was completed over a period of about a million years.

4. 300 to 200 billion years ago: The establishment and official registration of Nebadon

300 billion years ago: When the Andronover solar circuits had become stabilized and Michael's staff had arrived on Salvington, the Uversa government of Orvonton extended physical recognition to the local universe of Nebadon.

200 billion years ago: The completed universe machinery of Nebadon began to function regularly, and Nebadon was officially registered in the archives of Uversa as an evolutionary universe for the habitation of intelligent creatures and the ascension of mortals.

q090.question: Why did God allow evil to exist in the world?
q090.answer:
God did not create evil. To put it more precisely, evil is not a reality. In other words, it makes no sense to talk about whether or not it was created. It simply has no existence. Evil is like darkness. Darkness is not something real; it is merely the absence of light. When even a single small candle is brought in, the darkness vanishes to that extent.

As for the question of why evil exists in this world and why an almighty God permits evil, it is not that God permits evil; rather, the light of God is obscured by human ignorance and self-righteousness, producing a state of darkness. Strictly speaking, this is not even a matter of free will. It is not that human beings create some evil by their free will and remain in it; they are simply in a place where the Father's light, or to spell it out, truth, beauty, and goodness, is absent. That is why anyone can easily become an evildoer. The point is that one can become an evildoer not by actively creating evil but simply by not doing good.

In the story of Lucifer as well, it was not that Lucifer did evil but that he did not do good. He denied the existence of God, asserted his own unwarranted liberty, and lured many beings into that license.

The way to overcome evil is also self-evident. The way to overcome evil is not to repent, undergo ascetic discipline, and strive to cut evil off, but to receive the light of God, do good, seek truth, and realize beauty.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

In-Depth Summary: Evil as the Absence of Light and the Active Practice of Good

Preface: The Cosmic Dialectic of Light and Shadow

In the intellectual history of humankind, the inquiry into the origin and nature of evil and its solution has continued unceasingly under the name of theodicy. The question "Why does evil exist in a universe where an almighty and good God exists?" has been a central problem of the philosophy of religion from ancient times to the present. This essay examines the thesis stated above, namely the insight that "God did not create evil; evil is not a reality but a state like darkness in which light (truth, beauty, and goodness) is lacking; and the way to overcome it lies not in struggle but in receiving the light and practicing good," through the cosmology and theological system of The Urantia Book.

It surveys the classification of evil presented in The Urantia Book (error, evil, sin, and iniquity), sheds light on the conflict between false liberty and true liberty through the Lucifer rebellion, and sets forth the way of "⟦Q 194:3.12⟧overcoming evil with good⟦/Q⟧" shown in the life and teachings of Jesus.

1. Divine Perfection and the Structure of a Finite Universe

1.1 The Nature of God, the First Source and Center, and the Absence of Evil

The great premise of The Urantia Book is the absolute goodness and perfection of God. God is the personal source of truth, beauty, and goodness, and the book says that "⟦Q 130:1.5⟧there is absolutely no place in him for negative evil⟦/Q⟧." This strongly supports the first thesis, that "God did not create evil."

If God is absolute light, evil cannot come from him. The central universe of Havona, created by God, is perfect and eternal, and evil is contained neither in the divine nature nor in the original intention of creation. Evil is a by-product arising not from the Creator but in the experiential evolutionary process of imperfect creatures. God did not create evil; he created the opportunity for beings with free will to progress by their own efforts, and in this process the possibility of potential evil, imperfection, was opened up.

1.2 The Inevitability of Potential Evil and the Relativity of Time and Space

The Urantia Book strictly distinguishes between potential evil and actual evil. Potential evil is inherent in the imperfection that inevitably arises when the infinite and eternal is expressed in limited form in time and space. When the infinite God created a finite universe and placed within it beings of finite intelligence, that very finiteness already harbored imperfection, and this becomes the soil of potential evil.

From this point of view, evil is not an independent reality but a shadow arising from the relativity of reality. The very fact that the part stands before the whole constitutes the relativity of reality, and this creates the need for intellectual choice. God desired not mechanical robots but personal beings who could choose and love of their own accord. For freedom of choice to exist, the possibility of choosing the divine will (good) must logically be accompanied by the possibility of choosing what is not the divine will (the potential of evil). Therefore the possibility of evil is the price of the freedom given to free-willed creatures and the necessary background of cosmic growth.

1.3 Darkness as the Absence of Light: The Unreality of Evil

The insight that "evil is not a reality but a state like darkness in which there is no light" agrees with the ontology of The Urantia Book. In Paper 130, Jesus explains evil as immature choosing and an unthinking misstep, and emphasizes that God is so positively good that there is no room for negative evil.

Darkness is not an antiparticle of light particles. Physically speaking, darkness is simply the absence of photons. In the same way, in the cosmology of The Urantia Book, reality consists of truth (the intellectual dimension), beauty (the physical and artistic dimension), and goodness (the moral and spiritual dimension), and these three values are attributes of God. Therefore to move away from God (the light) or to reject him is to move away from reality and to enter the realm of unreality, that is, of shadow and darkness.

Evil originates in the misuse, distortion, and perversion of the finite. Evil is not a self-existent force but a derivative phenomenon that arises when finite beings obscure or distort the divine light. The clearer the divine reality, the more distinctly the act of rejecting it shows up as darkness, but that shadow can never overcome the light, and when the light shines it vanishes at once.

2. The Four Stages of Negativity: Error, Evil, Sin, and Iniquity

The Urantia Book does not speak of evil in a lump but distinguishes four stages, error, evil, sin, and iniquity, according to the intention and spiritual maturity of the creature. This classification is a decisive basis for upholding the thesis that "God did not create evil" and for clarifying human responsibility.

2.1 Error: The Lack of Intellectual Insight

Error, the most basic stage, arises not from deliberate rejection of truth but from a lack of intellectual keenness or from misunderstanding and distorting reality. Evolving human beings by nature start from ignorance and advance toward wisdom. The errors of judgment and immature understanding in this process are not objects of moral condemnation but part of the cosmic learning process.

Nature: intellectual immaturity
State: placed in the conflict between truth and untruth
Responsibility: no moral guilt, but correction is needed

2.2 Evil: The Lack of Wisdom and Disharmony

Evil is the partial realization of, or maladjustment to, universe realities and signifies a lack of wisdom. Imperfections in the natural order, misuse of plans, and maladjustment of techniques belong here.

Evil is inherent in the natural order of this world. This does not mean that God made evil; it means that, because evolution in time and space is itself a process of advancing from imperfection to perfection, its intermediate stages inevitably include discord. A lion hunting its prey may be a natural disharmony, but it is not a moral sin. Likewise, when a person causes others pain through unintended immaturity, this is classified as evil, but it does not thereby mean spiritual disconnection (sin).

Nature: cosmic maladjustment, lack of wisdom
State: a by-product of incomplete evolution
Significance: a background for growth and something to be overcome

2.3 Sin: The Deliberate Rejection of Light

From here on, "the state in which there is no light" combines with free will to bring about fatal spiritual consequences. Sin is conscious and deliberate transgression of divine law. If evil is a lack of wisdom, sin is spiritual poverty.

The deliberate choosing of evil constitutes sin. Sin is the attitude of knowingly choosing darkness and rejecting spiritual progress while knowing what is right and wrong. God allowed the possibility of evil for the sake of free will, but sin arises wholly when the creature resolves to shut out the light in his own mind. Sin is the product of a knowing mind dominated by an unsubmissive will.

2.4 Iniquity: The Disintegration of Personality and Cosmic Insanity

Iniquity, the most serious stage, is the continued pursuit of sin and error and the loss of personality control. This is not a mere mistake but open and persistent rebellion against cosmic reality.

A being sunk in iniquity places himself above the laws of the universe and finally severs every connection with reality (God). The Urantia Book describes this as a state close to cosmic insanity. It is the stage at which one goes beyond rejecting the light to believe that darkness is reality and to become one with the darkness. When this stage is reached, that personality loses its reality and ends in nonexistence (see Section 6).

Comparison of the Four Stages

Error: distortion of reality, misunderstanding rather than rejection of truth / cause: lack of intellectual keenness / intellectual immaturity
Evil: partial realization of, or maladjustment to, universe reality / cause: lack of wisdom / cosmic disharmony
Sin: deliberate transgression of divine law / cause: spiritual poverty, disobedience / intentional rebellion
Iniquity: continued pursuit of sin, persistent rejection of reality / cause: loss of personality control / cosmic insanity, self-destruction

3. Liberty and License: The Origin of Evil Seen in the Lucifer Rebellion

The most powerful example demonstrating historically the thesis that "God did not create evil" is the Lucifer rebellion. This event shows how a being created perfect produced evil by choosing darkness of his own accord.

3.1 The Fall of Lucifer: The Arrogance of Self-Assertion

Lucifer was originally a primary Lanonandek Son outstanding in wisdom, brilliance, and efficiency, and the Sovereign of the system of Satania. He was created perfect, yet, as the record says, "⟦Q 53:1.1⟧You were perfect in all your ways from the day you were created till unrighteousness was found in you⟦/Q⟧," he walked the path of downfall by his own free will.

The central cause of the rebellion was not outside temptation or any defect but self-assertion and the sophistry of false personal liberty that began within Lucifer himself. He refused loyalty to the Universal Father and the Creator Son and began to place the self at the center of the universe. This is the prototype of the act of turning one's back on the light and producing darkness.

3.2 False Liberty (License) and True Liberty

Lucifer justified the rebellion by his so-called declaration of liberty. He asserted that the Universal Father was a myth who did not exist and agitated that every intelligent being should have the liberty of self-determination. The Urantia Book, however, defines this as license.

True liberty: associated with genuine self-respect and the fruit of self-control. It recognizes cosmic relationships and is realized through love and service.
False liberty (license): the counterpart of self-admiration and the mask of unbridled self-assertion. It infringes on the rights of others, ignores cosmic obligations, and ends in abject bondage.

Lucifer misused the free will that God had given him and produced disharmony and rebellion in the name of liberty. Evil is not a creation of God but a distorted state produced by creatures through the misuse of their own liberty.

3.3 God's Response: Permission Rather Than Immediate Suppression

When Lucifer rebelled, the universe authorities did not immediately suppress him by force. Instead of destroying evil by force, Michael chose a wise delay so that the rebellion would reveal its own contradictions. This accords with the thesis that "fighting evil is not the solution." By letting evil reveal its own falsity and destructiveness, God enabled every being in the universe to distinguish good from evil and to choose the light for himself.

4. The Phenomenology of Light: Truth, Beauty, and Goodness and the Unreality of Evil

4.1 Truth, Beauty, and Goodness

The Urantia Book explains cosmic reality in terms of the three dimensions of truth, beauty, and goodness.

Truth: the recognition of God on the intellectual level
Beauty: harmony on the physical and artistic level
Goodness: divine personality on the moral and spiritual level

Truth, beauty, and goodness come from God, who is the personality of love. Therefore to live in these three values is to live in reality, in the light. Evil, on the other hand, is the state in which these three values are lacking. Evil is merely the distortion of truth (error), the destruction of beauty (ugliness), and the rejection of goodness (sin); it is not a reality in its own right.

4.2 The Analogy of the Shadow: Fear without Substance

As in the analogy that "⟦Q 195:5.12⟧the black patches of evil which you see are shown against a white background of ultimate good⟦/Q⟧," a shadow is merely a phenomenon that arises when light is blocked by an object; the shadow itself has no power to extinguish or attack the light.

Many ancient religions and dualistic philosophies have raised evil to a power equal to good, but The Urantia Book firmly rejects this. What we feel as evil is a relative deficiency that arises when the infinite light of God does not fully shine into the lives of finite mortals. Therefore the right attitude toward evil is not to fence with the shadow but to shine light into that place.

5. The Way of Overcoming Evil with Good

The central claim that "the way to overcome evil is not to fight evil but to receive the light of God and do good" is gathered up in the teachings of Jesus. This is not passive avoidance but the most powerful and active spiritual attitude.

5.1 Jesus' Method: A New Love Drives Out the Old

Jesus taught not to yield passively to evil but to respond swiftly and actively with good in order to overcome evil with good. This resembles what Thomas Chalmers called "the expulsive power of a new affection." If one tries forcibly to drive out the darkness within the mind, the mind becomes empty, and evil easily takes up residence again in an empty mind. If instead one fills the mind with the love of God and good deeds, evil naturally loses its place.

What is truly good is always stronger than the most malignant evil. Jesus taught, "Resist not evil," warning against becoming tainted unawares with the ways of evil (hatred, anger, violence) in the course of fighting it. Instead he emphasized that the way of the citizens of the heavenly kingdom is to render evil powerless by the overwhelming positiveness of practicing good.

5.2 The Sin of Omission and Spiritual Stagnation

The Urantia Book emphasizes that it is not enough merely to refrain from doing wrong. This is a warning against failing to do good when one could.

Primitive religion stopped at the negative goodness of keeping taboos, but the religion of Jesus is founded on the positive command "Go and do good." Spiritual stagnation is a shortcut to evil. As water that does not flow goes stale, a soul that stops and does no good loses its inner light and is eaten away by darkness.

The way out of inaction is to exercise the power of living faith. The Urantia Book calls not for recluses who hide to avoid evil but for believers in the kingdom who actively serve and practice love in the midst of the world. At the very moment one does good, the evil in that place disappears.

5.3 The Armor of Faith

Faith is an effective armor against sin and iniquity. The Urantia Book says that fallen spirits such as Satan and Caligastia have no power to invade or harass the faith sons of God.

When we receive the light of God (truth, beauty, and goodness) and abide in faith, we gain spiritual immunity to evil. It is not that we defeat outward evil by fighting it, but that the inner light becomes so strong that the outer darkness cannot seep in. Because God is love, there is no place in him for negative evil. When we become one with God, there is no longer any place for evil to dwell in us either.

Two Responses to Evil

Basic attitude: the worldly, dualistic way acknowledges evil as a reality and opposes it / Jesus' way regards evil as a shadow and does good
Method: resistance, revenge, repression, criticism / forgiveness, service, love, receiving the light
State of mind: anger, fear, tension / peace, assurance, joy
Result: a cycle of evil, exhaustion, further evil / the disappearance of evil, spiritual growth, salvation

6. The End of Evil: Adjudication and Extinction

What becomes of evil that rejects the light to the end? The Urantia Book denies the doctrine of eternal hellfire and presents extinction instead. This confirms, finally, the thesis that evil is unreal.

6.1 The Loss of Reality and Nonexistence

Beings who persist in evil and iniquity cut themselves off from cosmic reality (God). Since God alone is the source of life, a being who has severed himself from that source loses the power to continue existing eternally. Complete identification with iniquity is equivalent to nonexistence.

Such beings are not actively punished by God; they meet the extinction of their existence as the inevitable consequence of their own choice. As a shadow disappears in a place full of light, those beings who rejected the light "become as though they had not been." Evil is not a reality that opposes good eternally but a temporary and illusory state.

6.2 The Harmony of Mercy and Justice

Yet until such extinction takes place, God in his infinite mercy gives every being the opportunity to return to the light. God loves the wicked and is always kind even to the ungrateful. Salvation is open to all who receive the light of God (faith) and reflect that light by doing good to their neighbors (service).

Conclusion: The Active Choice for Light Is Salvation

The nature of creation: God is perfect goodness and did not create evil. Evil is a potential side effect, a state of deficiency of light, arising in the evolutionary process of finite creatures endowed with free will.

The unreality of evil: Evil is only the distorted shadow of the cosmic realities of truth, beauty, and goodness; it is not a self-existent reality.

The way of salvation: The true way to overcome evil is not a war of attrition against darkness but the active practice of love, receiving the light of God within and doing good without.

Do not fear the shadow; walk toward the sun. When we walk toward the sun, the shadow falls behind us of its own accord. To receive the light of God and to do good: this is the secret of the final victory over evil and the way that leads to eternal life.

q091.question: Minority salvation vs. majority salvation
q091.answer:
The Timing and Nature of Salvation: Minority Salvation, Majority Salvation, and a Third Way

1. Introduction: The Central Issue in the Doctrine of Salvation

1.1 The Issue

Among readers of The Urantia Book there is an important doctrinal debate over when and how the ultimate destiny of mortals is decided. This debate can be summed up broadly as two views: minority salvation and majority (universal) salvation.

Minority salvation (the this-life determinism view): It holds that the eternal destiny of the mortal, that is, survival or extinction, is decided entirely by the choices made and the attainment of faith during the material life in this world. A mortal who fails to qualify for survival in this life cannot be resurrected at all, and his existence is simply extinguished.

Majority salvation (the universal resurrection view): It holds that, with very few exceptions, nearly all mortals are first resurrected into the morontia world. Life in this world is merely a preliminary stage, and a second chance, or the real chance, to choose one's ultimate destiny is given in the morontia world.

1.2 A New Hypothesis: A Third Way

This essay adopts a third perspective as a framework for critically examining the two extreme views. In the light of a Paradise journey that may extend to hundreds of millions of years, the minority-salvation claim that a fleeting life of a hundred years in this world, spent in confusion and ignorance, decides eternal extinction has a fundamental problem of proportionality. Such a conclusion does not seem plausible in view of the circumstances of divine justice.

The core of this hypothesis is that resurrection is not the completion or reward of salvation but the beginning of judgment, or of a new opportunity. This also accords with the biblical concepts of "the resurrection of judgment" and "⟦Q 188:3.9⟧the resurrection of life⟦/Q⟧." From this perspective, extinction is not a momentary failure in this world but the accumulated result of a conscious and final rejection of survival made over a sufficient period of time, including life in the morontia world.

1.3 Purpose and Scope

This essay examines the textual grounds and logical limitations of minority salvation and majority salvation respectively, points out the limitations of the two views, and then sets out the texts and reasoning that support the third way, that "resurrection is a continuation of opportunity, and extinction is a final choice."

2. The Grounds and Limitations of Minority Salvation (This-Life Determinism)

2.1 Textual Grounds

Minority salvation rests on several passages suggesting that mortal survival is not automatic or universal but conditional, and that its conditions must be met during this life.

Conditional survival: 40:5.19 clearly states the conditions of survival: "⟦Q 40:5.19⟧All souls of every possible phase of mortal existence will survive provided they manifest willingness to co-operate with their indwelling Adjusters and exhibit a desire to find God and to attain divine perfection, even though these desires be but the first faint flickers⟦/Q⟧..." Proponents of majority salvation focus on the minimal standard of "⟦Q 40:5.19⟧the first faint flickers⟦/Q⟧," but proponents of minority salvation emphasize that the heart of this passage lies in the clear preconditions of willingness and attitude. Survival, they say, is the result that follows when these preconditions are met.

Failure in this life: Several passages speak clearly of the possibility of failing to survive in this life. 16:9.3 uses the conditional "⟦Q 16:9.3⟧If mortal man fails to survive natural death⟦/Q⟧," which presupposes that there actually are cases of failing to survive at the point of natural death. Again, 113:2.4 states that "⟦Q 113:2.4⟧when human beings fail to survive⟦/Q⟧," their guardian seraphim "⟦Q 113:2.4⟧may repeatedly serve in similar capacities⟦/Q⟧." This suggests that failures to survive are not one-time occurrences.

The sentence of spiritual death: One of the strongest grounds for minority salvation is 112:3.2. This passage explains that when the mortal "⟦Q 112:3.2⟧has finally rejected survival⟦/Q⟧," he may be pronounced "⟦Q 112:3.2⟧spiritually insolvent, morontially bankrupt, in the conjoint opinion of the Adjuster and the surviving seraphim⟦/Q⟧." And such a death is declared to be "⟦Q 112:3.2⟧final in its significance irrespective of the temporary continuation of the living energies of the physical⟦/Q⟧..." This suggests that an individual's spiritual destiny can be finally decided even before physical death, and it becomes the central argument of this-life determinism.

Spiritual birth as a prerequisite: In 193:2.2 the risen Jesus says, "⟦Q 193:2.2⟧such survival is dependent on your having been previously born of the spirit of truth-seeking and God-finding⟦/Q⟧." Here the word "previously" strongly implies that spiritual birth must take place in this life as a prerequisite of survival, that is, of resurrection.

2.2 The Limitations of Minority Salvation

Despite these grounds, minority salvation faces serious philosophical and interpretive difficulties.

Philosophical limitation: The greatest limitation is the problem of proportionality mentioned above. If the divine plan includes an ascension journey to Paradise lasting hundreds of millions of years, how can the most confused, ignorant, and brief first stage of that plan, a fleeting hundred years, be the final test that justifies eternal extinction? This raises serious questions about the balance of divine justice and mercy.

Interpretive limitation: Minority salvation tends to inflate extreme cases such as 112:3.2 into a possibility of universal failure. The text seems clearly to distinguish passive failure due to ignorance or weakness from active rejection such as the final rejection of 112:3.2. 40:5.19 shows that the threshold of survival is very low ("⟦Q 40:5.19⟧the first faint flickers⟦/Q⟧"). If even faint flickers guarantee survival, the final rejection of 112:3.2 must mean not mere failure or a state of sin but an extreme spiritual state of consciously and stubbornly rejecting the light itself. Therefore 112:3.2 can apply not to a minority but only to a very small number of exceptional beings. Minority salvation can commit the logical error of inflating this possibility for a tiny few into a danger for the many.

3. The Grounds and Defects of Majority (Universal) Salvation (the Universal Resurrection View)

3.1 Textual Grounds

Majority salvation, which holds that nearly everyone is automatically resurrected into the morontia world, relies mainly on two passages and on particular interpretations of them.

Lucifer's claim: The key passage cited by supporters of this view is 53:3.5. There it is recorded that Lucifer "⟦Q 53:3.5⟧maintained that immortality was inherent in the system personalities, that resurrection was natural and automatic⟦/Q⟧." But this is only Lucifer's claim, and whether it is true or not cannot be known. The very fact that one must rely on a rebel's declaration to support a central doctrine of the revelation shows that there is no reliable textual evidence for this claim.

The new and living way: Another ground, 52:5.5, says that since Pentecost "⟦Q 52:5.5⟧Urantia mortals again may proceed directly to the morontia spheres⟦/Q⟧." Majority salvation reads this to mean that all mortals proceed directly to morontia. But this is a logical leap. The passage does not mean that the mortals who proceed to the morontia spheres are all mortals. That a way has been opened does not mean that everyone is automatically carried along it; it means only that qualified mortals have become able to ascend directly without waiting for the dispensational resurrection.

3.2 The Defect of Majority Salvation: Moral Laxity

The most serious problem with majority salvation is not only that its textual basis is weak but that it breeds spiritual laziness and moral laxity.

A personal testimony: "Even in my own case, after only a brief exposure to it, I actually found myself thinking, 'So all my hard work up to now was for nothing.'" This shows that majority salvation can immediately undermine the believer's sense of spiritual urgency and motivation for dedication.

The corruption of the attitude of faith: This doctrine carries a great risk of turning the active and dedicated attitude of "seek first the righteousness of God" into a passive and procrastinating attitude of "if I just live a good and diligent life, I suppose I will get the righteousness of God later on, in morontia." The rhetorical question "If we are told we get there for free, who would sacrifice and strive to seek?" pinpoints the fatal moral weakness of this doctrine.

Acts of faith made unnecessary: If everyone automatically enters the next stage, acts of faith in this life such as evangelism and repentance lose their importance. This can weaken the significance of death as a boundary and make the struggle of this life for spiritual growth meaningless.

3.3 Conclusion

Majority salvation, first, has so weak a textual basis that it must take a rebel's claim as its central ground; second, misreads 52:5.5; and third, has the moral weakness of undermining the central motivation of faith. It is therefore difficult to support either textually or morally.

4. Synthesis: Resurrection Is Opportunity, and Extinction Is a Final Choice

Between the harsh proportionality problem of minority salvation and the textual and moral weaknesses of majority salvation, the text provides reasoning that supports a third way. This perspective understands resurrection as the beginning of a process and extinction as the final result of conscious rejection.

4.1 The Nature of Resurrection: A Starting Line, Not a Finish Line

The key to resolving the contradictions of the two views lies in 47:3.7. This passage says that on the first mansion world "⟦Q 47:3.7⟧you will resume your intellectual training and spiritual development at the exact level whereon they were interrupted by death⟦/Q⟧," and that "⟦Q 47:3.7⟧You begin over there right where you leave off down here⟦/Q⟧."

This passage shows that resurrection is not a reward or an amnesty but a continuation.

If resurrection were final salvation or amnesty, as majority salvation claims, there would be no need to resume training.

If resurrection were a reward only for those who had already obtained salvation in this life, as minority salvation claims, the idea of beginning again right where one left off would be unnecessary, since they would already be in a state of spiritual attainment.

The text shows that resurrection continues the mortal's testing process in a new environment (morontia) in which material limitations have been removed. This agrees with the hypothesis that "resurrection is the beginning of opportunity" and solves the hundred-year proportionality problem that minority salvation could not solve. The hundred years of this life are only the first stage of testing, and through resurrection the second stage of testing (the morontia life) begins again at the very level at which it stopped in this life.

4.2 The Nature of Extinction: Conscious Rejection, Not Failure

The second pillar supporting the third way is a redefinition of the cause of extinction. The text consistently shows that extinction results not from the failure of an ignorant hundred years but from a conscious rejection confirmed over time.

146:2.5: "⟦Q 146:2.5⟧Even the infinite love of God cannot force the salvation of eternal survival upon any mortal creature who does not choose to survive⟦/Q⟧." This suggests that extinction is not a capricious punishment by God but the result of respecting the creature's free will to the very end.

196:3.35: "⟦Q 196:3.35⟧If man does not choose to survive⟦/Q⟧..." This passage too defines extinction not as passive failure but as a matter of active choice.

112:3.2: Although it is also used as a ground for minority salvation, it identifies the cause as when the mortal "⟦Q 112:3.2⟧has finally rejected survival⟦/Q⟧," emphasizing a final and conscious rejection rather than temporary wandering or ignorance.

47:2.7: Even in the case of children, regarding the ascendant career, it says that if they "⟦Q 47:2.7⟧definitely decide against the Havona adventure ... there is no resurrection from such a second death⟦/Q⟧."

What appears consistently in these four passages is not passive failure or ignorance but an active, volitional, and final rejection ("does not choose to survive," "does not choose," "finally rejected," "definitely decide"). This directly refutes the hundred-year failure model and supports the view that extinction is the result of a fundamental choice about existence.

4.3 The Nature of Adjudication: Sufficient Time and Self-Approval, Not Summary Judgment

The passages explaining the principles of divine adjudication provide the final reasoning that completes the third way.

54:3.2 says that between the cause, conscious identification with evil, and the result, the execution of the penalty, there must always intervene "⟦Q 54:3.2⟧a period of time of sufficient length⟦/Q⟧."

That time is needed so that the adjudication may win the victory of being "⟦Q 54:3.2⟧so fair and just as to win the approval of the sinner himself⟦/Q⟧."

This concept of the approval of the sinner himself shows the deepest aspect of divine justice.

The great majority of mortals who die in ignorance and confusion in this life have not had this sufficient time.

Such mortals are not in a spiritual and intellectual state in which they could themselves approve their own eternal extinction.

Therefore minority salvation, which holds that one is extinguished for falling short of attainment at the very moment of death in this life, in most cases contradicts the principle of divine justice set forth in 54:3.2.

Where, then, does the mortal obtain this sufficient time? The answer is the morontia life, the continuation of training, of which 47:3.7 speaks.

Taken together, these texts yield the following consistent model. Resurrection (47:3.7) is an opportunity given to nearly all mortals and is the divine provision that grants the sufficient time required by 54:3.2. During this time the mortal either continues the ascent or makes clear his final rejection (112:3.2) and thus ultimately approves his own destiny himself (54:3.2).

5. Conclusion: Integrating Faith in This Life and the Morontia Journey

5.1 The Third Way

The text appears to reject both the strict determinism of minority salvation and the moral permissiveness implied by majority salvation. The third way, the most consistent model, can be summarized as follows.

The role of this life: Life in this world is not a final examination but a qualifying examination. According to 40:5.19, qualification for survival is obtained merely by a "⟦Q 40:5.19⟧desire to find God⟦/Q⟧ ..." and "⟦Q 40:5.19⟧the first faint flickers⟦/Q⟧" of the true light. This threshold has been set deliberately very low by divine mercy.

The role of resurrection: Nearly all mortals who possess even these faint flickers are resurrected. But this resurrection is not the completion of salvation; it is entry into a field of opportunity (morontia) in which, as stated in 47:3.7, spiritual training begins again from that very point.

The role of extinction: Extinction is not an immediate punishment for failure in this life. It happens only to beings who finally reject even the additional opportunity given through resurrection (112:3.2), who choose not to wish to survive (146:2.5, 196:3.35), and who, after sufficient time has been given (54:3.2), themselves approve their own destiny. It is not an act of divine mercy but the final event in which the free will of the creature reaches completion.

5.2 Answer to the Question

The judgment that it "doesn't seem right, given the circumstances," that salvation and extinction should be decided by a hundred-year life that is "no more than a moment" is, in the light of textual analysis, entirely reasonable.

Extinction is not a hundred-year failure; as 146:2.5 and 54:3.2 strongly imply, it is itself the process of conscious and voluntary rejection of existence carried on over a sufficient period of time that includes the morontia life. Resurrection (47:3.7) is the divine field of opportunity given so that this very process may be continued and developed or, by one's own choice, brought to an end.

5.3 Comparison of the Three Views of Salvation

Minority salvation
Role of this life: final decision. The testing ground where eternal destiny is decided.
Nature of resurrection: final reward. Only those who obtained survival in this life are resurrected.
Cause of extinction: failure in this life. Falling short of the standard of faith or spiritual attainment.
Key grounds: 16:9.3, 112:3.2, 113:2.4, 193:2.2
Main limitation: the problem of proportionality. The problem of justice in a momentary life deciding eternity.

Majority salvation
Role of this life: a formal process. Life in this world has almost no effect on final destiny.
Nature of resurrection: a universal and automatic process. Nearly everyone is resurrected and receives the real opportunity.
Cause of extinction: failure in morontia (or it almost never happens).
Key grounds: 53:3.5 (Lucifer's claim), 52:5.5 (misread)
Main limitation: moral laxity ("So all my hard work up to now was for nothing"). It undermines the motivation for faith and repentance, and its textual basis is very weak.

Integrated perspective (the third way)
Role of this life: qualification. The first stage, in which the will to survive (the "faint flickers") is established.
Nature of resurrection: a continuation of opportunity. The field in which spiritual training is resumed from the point where it stopped in this life.
Cause of extinction: final rejection. Choosing over a sufficient period of time not to wish to survive and oneself approving that decision.
Key grounds: 47:3.7, 40:5.19, 146:2.5, 54:3.2, 196:3.35
Main limitation: not so much a textual limitation as the complexity of requiring an integrated understanding between the two extremes.

q092.question: The Urantia Book's view of reincarnation: what are memories of past lives?
q092.answer:
The Urantia Book's View of Reincarnation: A Critique of Reincarnation and a Reinterpretation of "Past-Life Memories"

1. Introduction: The Uniqueness of Personality and Eternal One-Directional Ascent

The two most fundamental pillars of the cosmology of The Urantia Book are the uniqueness of personality and an ascent that moves in one direction. Every mortal possesses personality, an irreplaceable and unique gift received from the Universal Father. This personality stands before a single, magnificent opportunity for eternal survival and before the choices of free will.

This view of the universe is essentially based on progressive order and one-directional development, and it stands in clear contrast to the cyclical model of "eternal recurrence." Therefore the idea of transmigration or reincarnation is regarded not merely as a difference of doctrine but as a denial of the most fundamental premise of The Urantia Book, namely the unique worth of the being called "you" and the very purpose of the cosmic journey.

On the basis of the text of The Urantia Book, this essay seeks, first, to set out the reasons why it clearly rejects the idea of reincarnation and, second, to reinterpret, in terms of the concepts of The Urantia Book, the phenomenon of "past-life memories" commonly offered as evidence of reincarnation, showing that it is not the recycling of personality but the inheritance of cosmic experience.

2. The Rejection of Reincarnation in the Text of The Urantia Book

The Urantia Book regards reincarnation not as a mere philosophical error but as a serious obstacle blocking the spiritual progress of mortals. This is clearly seen in the records concerning Melchizedek, Jesus, and Gautama Siddhartha.

2.1 The "Stultifying" Doctrine (94:2.3)

The Melchizedek author sharply criticizes the harm of the idea of reincarnation. He declares that nothing was so stultifying as the doctrine of the reincarnation of souls that came from the Dravidian Deccan.

This doctrine is stultifying because it robbed mortals of the hope of finding deliverance and spiritual advancement through death. In The Urantia Book, death is a deliverance and a graduation into the next stage of the eternal ascension career. But the doctrine of transmigration turned this hope into a fear of a weary and monotonous round of repeated rebirths.

Such a philosophy finally led to a doctrine of the complete annihilation of the self (union with Brahman), and in the process mortal desire and human ambition collapsed. The Urantia Book regards spiritual ambition and the divine discontent that drives toward progress as the motive power of the Paradise ascent. The doctrine of transmigration, by contrast, is criticized for removing this motive power, making mortals resigned, and binding them in spiritual despair.

2.2 Jesus and Gautama (130:2.8, 94:7.3)

Jesus clearly denied the form of reincarnation in which a human soul is reborn in the body of an animal. When Ganid saw an intelligent shepherd dog and asked whether the dog had a soul, Jesus explained that because the dog cannot know God, who is spirit, it cannot experience anything like eternal personality survival. From that day on Ganid never again held the belief that the souls of men transmigrate into the bodies of animals.

The case of Gautama Siddhartha is even more interesting. The Urantia Book criticizes Gautama for failing to perceive the reality of the individual soul, yet it speaks favorably of his valiant fight against the time-honored belief in the transmigration of the soul. Gautama diagnosed the disease of transmigration correctly, but he prescribed the extreme remedy of denying the individual soul itself. The Urantia Book supports his conclusion that "transmigration is wrong" but rejects his premise that "there is no individual soul," and it offers instead the alternative of the eternal ascent of the individual soul.

2.3 Anthropological Origin: A Misunderstanding of Primitive Observation (86:4.6)

The Urantia Book regards the origin of the idea of reincarnation not as some mysterious ancient wisdom but as a misunderstanding of primitive observation. The orange race was especially given to belief in transmigration and reincarnation, and the book explains that this idea of reincarnation originated in the observation that offspring resemble their ancestors in traits and hereditary characteristics.

In days when genetics was unknown, people saw a grandson who resembled his grandfather and believed that the grandfather's soul had returned; this, it says, was the beginning of the idea of reincarnation. The Urantia Book also regards this belief as a residue of Adam's teachings about the mansion worlds that had become contaminated.

3. Repeating Kindergarten (Reincarnation) versus Going on to College (Ascension)
